facts.statement: Caypullisaurus is an extinct genus of large ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur that lived in Argentina during the Late Jurassic and Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Caypullisaurus is an extinct genus of platypterygiine ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous (Tithonian and Berriasian stages) of Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Marta Fernández in 1997, with the type species designated as Caypullisaurus bonapartei.
facts.quote: Caypullisaurus was first named by Marta Fernández in 1997 and the type species is Caypullisaurus bonapartei.

facts.statement: Caypullisaurus was a large ichthyosaur that measured approximately 7 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a large ichthyosaur, measuring about 7 m long.

facts.statement: The forelimbs of Caypullisaurus possessed 10 digits each.
facts.quote: The forelimbs of Caypullisaurus contained 10 digits each.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was found in the Vaca Muerta Formation of Cerro Lotena, Neuquén, dating to the early Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its holotype was collected from the Vaca Muerta Formation of Cerro Lotena, Neuquen, dating to the early Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic, about 150 million years ago.

facts.statement: Caypullisaurus belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae and is closely related to the genera Platypterygius and Brachypterygius.
facts.quote: It is a member of the family Ophthalmosauridae, and closely related to Platypterygius and Brachypterygius.

facts.statement: A 2012 analysis found Caypullisaurus to be most closely related to Athabascasaurus and "Platypterygius" australis, placing it within the subfamily Platypterygiinae.
facts.quote: In 2012, Caypullisaurus was found to be most closely related to Athabascasaurus and "Platypterygius" australis, and to nest within the subfamily Platypterygiinae.

facts.statement: Caypullisaurus lived between 145.06 and 137.05 million years ago, spanning the Tithonian and Berriasian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Berriasian (145.06 to 137.05 million years ago)
